summary.text: John Hickenlooper is the Democratic incumbent seeking a second term in the U.S. Senate. A geologist who opened Colorado's first brewpub, he served as Mayor of Denver (2003-2011) and Governor of Colorado (2011-2019), briefly sought the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination, and won his Senate seat in 2020. He won the June 2026 Democratic primary over state Sen. Julie Gonzales.

paragraphs.text: Born in Narberth, Pennsylvania, in 1952. His Senate biography says he was raised by his single mother after his father died of cancer when he was eight.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1974) and a master's degree in geology (1980) from Wesleyan University.

Started his career in Colorado as a geologist, including work with Buckhorn Petroleum. After being laid off in the mid-1980s recession, he opened the state's first brewpub in Denver's Lower Downtown (LoDo) warehouse district, and he and his partners went on to renovate historic buildings in Denver and other cities.

Was elected Mayor of Denver in 2003 and served until 2011. According to his Senate biography, his mayoralty included building the FasTracks transit system with the region's mayors, early childhood education for every 4-year-old in Denver, and police reforms.

Served as Governor of Colorado from 2011 to 2019. His Senate biography cites an expansion of health care coverage to half a million Coloradans, climate pollution limits, gun safety measures, and the first U.S. regulatory framework for legal recreational marijuana.
Announced a run for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination on March 4, 2019, and suspended the campaign on August 15, 2019.
Won election to the U.S. Senate in 2020, defeating incumbent Republican Cory Gardner. He took the seat in 2021.

Serves on the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Energy and Natural Resources; Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions; and Small Business and Entrepreneurship committees (2025-2026), and is ranking member of two subcommittees.
Defeated state Sen. Julie Gonzales in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, 52.8% to 47.2%.
